doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Advice, listening and the record business
title: Labels pushing guest artists and objecting to synthesizers
summary: Companies urged guests like Dexter Gordon and disliked the synthesizer of Mark Copeland, even for today's albums.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Did anybody ever tell you who you should use? Did they -- did anyone you recorded forever say, "I really -­
-- think you ought to work with -- I think you ought to bring this guy into -- ?

-- well, they wanted -- they wanted to do that, too. I want to make my album, they say, "Well, I think you outta have a guest artist." I says, "Yeah, I want to do it myself." Every time I look, they had me doing something with Dexter Gordon [phonetic sp.]. You know, like every time -- I say, "Godda -- I mean, dammit, why don't you let me do something?" Every time, I'm doing something with Dexter or Gene Hammond [phonetic sp.] or something, it's always, you know.
Was that when you were with Chess, or?
No, not with Chess. No, just in general.
Somebody's always calling me, you know, but when it comes for record dates -­
-- then, no, I mean, they'd get other people, you know.
You know, to record. You know. "Oh, Moody, you sound good, yeah," but -- but no, but this guy, he's got his quartet, he's got his quartet, they didn't want me to have 20 people
So on your date, they're trying to add people in -­
-- but on like Dexter's date, they're not calling you and saying, "Moody, why don't you come over and play on Dexter's date."

No, we'd like for you to be on Dexter's date, you know, so I'm on a couple albums with him. Yeah, so. But, man, like if they would just give my quartet a little shake and -- and would've just gone and pushed it, my quartet would've been accepted. And it'll still be accepted one day. They're telling me they don't like synthesizers. "The people don't like sy" -- what people? "Well, I -- they told me." I said, "Well, they told me they do." So, you know. I said, "It's not what the people like. I like it! I'm the one playing. It's my group. I like it! So I want that to be there." "Yeah, but we want a straight ahead album." That synthesizers -- and I got one of the best synthesizer players in the world, Mark Copeland, and they're talking about, you know.
